paragraphs: Recent studies suggest that remote work may improve employee productivity (Smith & Lee, 2021). However, the effect appears to depend on task type and supervisory support.
In a survey of 412 knowledge workers, 68% reported higher focus at home, yet 41% reported difficulty disconnecting after hours.
These findings indicate that productivity gains are conditional rather than universal.
Smith, J., & Lee, K. (2021). Remote work and productivity. Journal of Work, 12(3), 45-60.
